basis: Neuronal migration defect; supplied HPO reports bleeding/coagulopathy, pyloric stenosis and scoliosis in 80-99%. Cardiac defects (30-79%) omitted by cap; frequencies may vary across subtypes.
Defined by skeletal muscle hypertrophy; increased strength and reduced fat do not establish additional organ disease.
Malignant circulating plasma cells and marrow disease; renal impairment occurs in roughly 30-50% and lytic bone lesions in roughly 35-50%, varying by primary versus secondary disease.
Defining malformations affect external ears, finger phalanges and toenails; dermatoglyphic changes alone do not establish further damage.
Inherited excess red blood cell production; thrombosis risk does not establish common direct vascular damage across the umbrella.
Intermittent atrial cardiac rhythm disorder; stroke and heart failure are separate complications.
Isolated inherited oocyte maturation defect causing female infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Keratinopathic ichthyosis; structural eyelid dysfunction from ectropion occurs in 5/7 patients, with strabismus in 3/6.
Age-defined malignancy umbrella without a shared organ of origin; no organ axis can be assigned consistently across its subtypes.
Definition states no intrinsic phenotype; listed organ abnormalities reflect separately unmasked recessive diseases and cannot be attributed to maternal UPD4 itself.
Congenital glycosylation disorder causing muscular dystrophy and brain malformations; defining ocular damage includes retinal dysplasia in 20/20 patients.
Autoimmune cutaneous lupus localized to eyelid skin; eyelids fall within the ocular axis.
Benign tumour arising in subcutaneous tissue or deep soft connective tissue; both are explicitly stated sites of origin.
Unclassified leukodystrophy remains a disorder of central nervous system white matter; unspecified cause does not establish a metabolic axis.
Peroxisomal fatty/bile acid metabolic defect with defining encephalopathy and neuropathy; pigmentary retinopathy in 1/2 supports ocular damage. Infantile liver disease is rare.
Viral infection directly inflames the pericardium.
Necrosis directly destroys the pituitary endocrine gland; its intracranial location alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Isolated congenital facial nerve dysfunction; orbicularis weakness and reduced corneal reflex do not establish intrinsic ocular damage.
Carcinoma originates in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary invasion or obstruction is not intrinsic to every case.
Deglycosylation defect with neurodevelopmental disease and alacrima (12/15); hepatic injury is characteristic, with elevated transaminases in 8/11 (~73%).
Leishmania infects the reticuloendothelial system, characteristically involving spleen, marrow and liver, with anemia and hepatosplenomegaly.
Epithelial malignancy of the ovary is reproductive, without intrinsic endocrine dysfunction; metastatic organ involvement is not assumed.
Direct seventh cranial nerve injury causes facial paralysis; presumed viral triggers do not establish infection in all cases.
Intellectual disability, retinal dystrophy and truncal obesity define the syndrome; renal abnormalities are occasional (5-29%). Micropenis has no reproductive axis.
Inherited encephalopathy defines brain dysfunction; additional organ damage and metabolic mechanisms vary by subtype.
